walkthroughs.body_html:
Statistical Sampling — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Statistical Sampling brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Statistical Sampling.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What does it mean to solve a pair of simultaneous equations?
options: Add the two equations together and solve as if it were a single equation.
£24.50, by multiplying £3.50 by 7.
Find the values of the variables that satisfy both equations at the same time (the point where the two lines meet).
Solve each equation separately and write both sets of answers.

mcqs.q: If 5 pens cost £3.50, how much do 7 pens cost?
options: £5.50, by adding £2 to £3.50 because there are 2 more pens.
They add up to 360 degrees because they make a full turn.
£4.90 — find the unit cost (£0.70 per pen), then multiply by 7.
£24.50, by multiplying £3.50 by 7.

mcqs.q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. What is the relationship between co-interior (allied) angles?
options: They add up to 360 degrees because they make a full turn.
They are equal to each other, like alternate angles.
£24.50, by multiplying £3.50 by 7.
They add up to 180 degrees.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Discrete vs continuous”?
options: E(aX + b) = aE(X) + b; Var(aX + b) = a²Var(X). For independent X, Y: Var(X+Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y).
PMF p(x) gives P(X = x) for discrete X. Σp(x) = 1. Used to define distribution.
Discrete: countable outcomes (binomial, Poisson). Continuous: any value in an interval (normal, exponential).
E(X) = Σx·p(x) (discrete) or ∫x·f(x) dx (continuous). Long-run average value.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Linear combinations”?
options: E(X) = Σx·p(x) (discrete) or ∫x·f(x) dx (continuous). Long-run average value.
E(aX + b) = aE(X) + b; Var(aX + b) = a²Var(X). For independent X, Y: Var(X+Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y).
PDF f(x) for continuous X. P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx. Total area under curve = 1.
PMF p(x) gives P(X = x) for discrete X. Σp(x) = 1. Used to define distribution.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Probability density function”?
options: PMF p(x) gives P(X = x) for discrete X. Σp(x) = 1. Used to define distribution.
PDF f(x) for continuous X. P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx. Total area under curve = 1.
Var(X) = E(X²) − [E(X)]². Spread of distribution. SD = √Var(X).
E(aX + b) = aE(X) + b; Var(aX + b) = a²Var(X). For independent X, Y: Var(X+Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y).
